findings.recommendation: Validate the selected fields needed for the observation while stripping/ignoring unrelated provider fields, or provide a versioned documented synthetic subset contract and revise the acceptance criterion to avoid implying provider-shaped messages.
findings.failure_mode: The schema applies strict rejection to the outer data object and order object while modeling only a small subset of their fields. Alpaca documents trade_updates.data messages with fields such as execution_id and an order object carrying fields including asset_class, asset_id, created_at, updated_at, submitted_at, filled_at, order_class, order_type, time_in_force, limit_price, and extended_hours. A documented provider-shaped message therefore fails validation before the selected fields can be normalized; the handcrafted minimal test fixture does not cover this realistic payload.
findings.evidence: Official Alpaca Websocket Streaming docs state trade_updates order is the same object returned from REST and show a full order object plus execution_id: https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/websocket-streaming . The candidate schema makes these extra properties invalid at lines 23-37.
findings.requirement: Valid synthetic provider-shaped trade updates must be accepted and normalized.
